Comp.name: Threshold
Comp.desc: Level where compression starts. The fader sits over the input meter

Comp.name: Ratio
Comp.desc: How strongly levels above Threshold are reduced

Comp.name: Knee
Comp.desc: How gradually compression starts

Comp.name: Weird
Comp.desc: An alternative knee that starts at Threshold, so compression arrives later and then catches up

Comp.name: Attack
Comp.desc: How quickly compression engages

Comp.name: Classic
Comp.desc: Puts attack and release on the detector, as older compressors do. Short peaks then get less reduction with a long attack. With it off, attack doesn't change the maximum reduction

Comp.name: Release
Comp.desc: How quickly it lets go

Comp.name: Auto
Comp.desc: Program-dependent release: fast after transients, slower after sustained compression

Comp.name: Pre-comp
Comp.desc: Lookahead, so compression can start before a transient arrives

Comp.name: RMS size
Comp.desc: Averaging time of the detector. 0 ms is peak detection

Comp.name: Wet
Comp.desc: Level of the compressed signal

Comp.name: Dry
Comp.desc: Level of the uncompressed signal, for parallel compression

Comp.name: Link channels
Comp.desc: Both channels share gain reduction, which keeps the stereo image steady

Comp.name: Auto make-up
Comp.desc: Adds back half of the gain reduction a full-scale signal would get

Comp.name: Limit output
Comp.desc: Turns on a brickwall limiter with a 0 dBFS ceiling. It adds 104 samples of latency

Comp.name: Oversampling
Comp.desc: 2x, 4x or 8x reduces aliasing at very fast settings and from Character, at the cost of CPU and latency. With it on, the detector always averages over at least 0.1 ms

Comp.name: Oversampling filter
Comp.desc: Linear keeps wet and dry phase-aligned. Minimum has less pre-ringing

Comp.name: Feedback detection
Comp.desc: The detector listens to the compressor's own output, for a gentler, more program-dependent response

Comp.name: Link amount
Comp.desc: How strongly linked channels follow the louder one

Comp.name: Release curve
Comp.desc: Linear falls at a constant dB rate, like older compressors

Comp.name: Attack = 90 % rise
Comp.desc: See below

Comp.name: Output
Comp.desc: The same control as the header knob

Comp.name: Drive
Comp.desc: How hard the curve is driven. Quiet material passes untouched, so turning Drive up rounds the peaks rather than making everything louder: at Drive 12 dB, peaks above about -12 dBFS are rounded and held near that level. Lower Threshold or raise Wet if the result is quieter than you want

Comp.name: Up threshold
Comp.desc: Level where compression starts. The fader sits over the input meter

Comp.name: Up ratio
Comp.desc: How strongly levels above Threshold are reduced

Comp.name: Hold
Comp.desc: The release waits this long after the last peak. With fast settings and peak detection, the gain otherwise follows each cycle of a low note, which is distortion: a Hold a little longer than the note's period (20 ms for 50 Hz) keeps it steady. The upward lift doesn't hold

Comp.name: Range
Comp.desc: The most gain reduction Comp will apply, 1 to 40 dB; Off is the top of the knob. With Auto threshold it makes a level rider that never pulls a passage down by more than Range. Auto make-up then adds back half of what Range allows, not half of what the curve would take

DS-Mini.name: Profile
DS-Mini.desc: What it listens for. The ‹ › arrows step through the profiles. The line under it shows the band

DS-Mini.name: Amount
DS-Mini.desc: How much it de-esses. 0 does nothing at all; 5 is moderate; 10 is strong

DS-Mini.name: Mode
DS-Mini.desc: Split turns down only the band. Wide turns down the whole signal, which can sound more natural on some voices

DS-Mini.name: Lookahead
DS-Mini.desc: Starts turning down 2 ms before an "s" arrives. Adds 2 ms of latency (96 samples at 48 kHz), which REAPER compensates

DS-Mini.name: Link channels
DS-Mini.desc: Both channels are turned down together, on the louder one

DS.name: Threshold
DS.desc: How loud the band must get before it's turned down

DS.name: Freq
DS.desc: The centre of the band, or where the shelf starts. Typed values take `6200` or `6.2k`

DS.name: Width
DS.desc: How wide the band is. Locked in Shelf

DS.name: Range
DS.desc: The most it ever turns down

DS.name: Attack
DS.desc: How fast the cut comes in

DS.name: Detector
DS.desc: What the detector listens to. Mid and Side catch sibilance in the centre or at the sides

DS.name: Link channels
DS.desc: Both channels get the same cut. Off, each side is de-essed on its own (Main input L+R and Sidechain L+R only)

DS.name: Lookahead
DS.desc: Delays the audio but not the detector, so the cut is already moving when an "s" arrives. Adds that much latency

DS.name: Split filter
DS.desc: Linear phase splits the band with linear-phase filters, so nothing around the band shifts in phase. Its band edges are steeper, so it takes a little less off the edges of an "s". Adds about 53 ms of latency

Delay.name: Feedback
Delay.desc: How much of each repeat comes back

Delay.name: Resolution
Delay.desc: Reduces bit depth for a lo-fi sound

Delay.name: Width
Delay.desc: 0 is mono, 1 is unchanged, above 1 is wider

Delay.name: Pan
Delay.desc: Balance, so the centre is unchanged and a hard pan silences the other side

Delay.name: Character
Delay.desc: Clean is the plain delay. Tape adds a soft saturation, a low bump around 90 Hz and a top end that dulls with every pass through the loop. BBD is a dark, band-limited bucket-brigade sound whose top falls as the time gets longer, with a faint noise that follows the signal

Delay.name: Amount
Delay.desc: How strong the character is. Unused on Clean

Delay.name: Mod rate
Delay.desc: Speed of the wow and flutter

Delay.name: Mod depth
Delay.desc: The peak pitch change. 0 is no modulation

Delay.name: Random
Delay.desc: How much of the motion is a slow random wander rather than a steady wobble

Delay.name: Diffusion
Delay.desc: Smears each repeat into the next inside the loop, so repeats turn into a wash

Delay.name: Duck amount
Delay.desc: How strong the character is. Unused on Clean

EQ.name: Type
EQ.range: Low shelf, High shelf, Band, Notch, Low pass, High pass, Band pass, All pass, Tilt
EQ.desc: The filter's shape

EQ.name: Freq
EQ.desc: Centre or corner frequency

EQ.name: Gain
EQ.desc: Boost or cut. The note in brackets is the one nearest Freq

EQ.name: Q
EQ.desc: Narrower as it rises. On pass filters and shelves, 0.707 is flat, and more adds a resonant peak

EQ.name: Slope
EQ.desc: For the selected band

EQ.name: Phase
EQ.desc: Linear keeps every frequency time-aligned, at the cost of latency. Use it for multi-mic or parallel work

EQ.name: FIR length
EQ.desc: Linear mode only. Longer holds low-frequency detail better and adds latency

EQ.name: Oversampling
EQ.desc: Minimum mode only. Rarely needed, because the filters already hold their shape

EQ.name: Log-scale automated freq.
EQ.desc: With it on, an automation envelope moves Freq evenly in octaves. With it off, it moves Freq evenly in Hz. Ticking it doesn't move any band, but existing Freq envelopes will then mean something different

EQ.name: Show grid
EQ.desc: The grid lines. The numbers always show

EQ.name: Show phase
EQ.desc: The total phase in yellow, with the graph's height being ±180°. It's flat in Linear mode

EQ.name: Compact mode
EQ.desc: Hides the lower panel, so the graph gets the room

EQ.name: Graph range
EQ.desc: Auto is ±12 dB, or ±18 dB in Compact mode

EQ.name: Analyzer
EQ.desc: Before or after the EQ. The graph's corner shows which

EQ.name: Pink tilt
EQ.desc: Adds 4.5 dB per octave about 1 kHz, so pink noise reads flat

EQ.name: Peak hold
EQ.desc: Adds a fainter line at the highest level. Turn it off to clear it

EQ.name: Smoothing
EQ.desc: How slowly the analyzer line moves

EQ.name: Threshold
EQ.desc: The level where the band starts to act. A sine's level is its RMS: a full-scale sine is -3 dB

EQ.name: Range
EQ.desc: How far the gain can move. Negative cuts, positive boosts. It's all used 12 dB past Threshold, with a soft start over the 6 dB around it

EQ.name: Attack
EQ.desc: How fast the band moves when it starts to act

EQ.name: Release
EQ.desc: How fast it goes back

EQ.name: Sidechain
EQ.desc: The band listens to the sidechain input instead of the main input

EQ.name: Channel
EQ.desc: What the analyzer shows. Mid is the two channels' sum, as before

Exciter.name: Freq
Exciter.desc: Only content above this is excited

Exciter.name: Clip Boost
Exciter.desc: How hard the signal drives the clipper. More gives denser harmonics

Exciter.name: Harmonics
Exciter.desc: How much of the excited signal is added. At 0 % the plugin changes nothing

Exciter.name: Mix Back
Exciter.desc: Overall level of the excited signal

Exciter.name: Oversampling
Exciter.desc: Reduces harsh aliasing, at the cost of CPU and latency

Exciter.name: Character
Exciter.desc: 0 % favours even harmonics, which sound warmer. 100 % gives odd harmonics only, which sound edgier

Exciter.name: Output
Exciter.desc: The same control as the header knob

FIR.name: Mode
FIR.range: EQ, Gate, Compressor, Subtract, Convolve L/R

FIR.name: Reduction
FIR.desc: The most any frequency is turned down

FIR.name: Offset
FIR.desc: Moves the profile. Higher removes more, and can thin the sound

FIR.name: Smoothing
FIR.desc: Smooths the reduction across time and frequency. Higher avoids "musical noise", the warbling bleeps of hard noise reduction

Gate.name: Hysteresis
Gate.desc: Where it closes, relative to Threshold

Gate.name: Lookahead
Gate.desc: Delays the audio by 50 ms, so the gate can open before the hit. Adds 50 ms latency, which REAPER compensates

Gate.name: Pre-open
Gate.desc: How early the gate starts to open, before the hit. Needs Lookahead

Gate.name: Hold
Gate.desc: How long it stays open after the level falls

Gate.name: Range
Gate.desc: How far the closed gate turns down. -inf is silence

Gate.name: RMS size
Gate.desc: How long the detector averages. 0 is peak detection

Gate.name: Mode
Gate.desc: Duck turns the signal down by Range while the detector is over Threshold

Gate.name: Link channels
Gate.desc: Both channels open together, on the louder one

Gate.name: Noise
Gate.desc: White noise, only while the gate is open. In Duck mode, while it ducks

Kicker.name: Filter Q
Kicker.desc: Width of the band. Higher is narrower and rings longer

Kicker.name: Output
Kicker.desc: The same control as the header knob

Kicker.name: Mono below Freq
Kicker.desc: Sums the input to the filter to mono, so the added low end is identical in both channels. The dry signal stays stereo

Kicker.name: Soft clip
Kicker.desc: Rounds peaks at the output so they can't exceed 0 dBFS. It starts acting at about -3 dBFS

Kicker.name: Cutoff
Kicker.desc: The highest frequency Sub listens to. Set it just above the kick's body

Kicker.name: Sub
Kicker.desc: The level of the sub it creates

Kicker.name: Sensitivity
Kicker.desc: Below this level Sub stays silent, so bleed and noise don't make sub

Kicker.name: Sub low-pass
Kicker.desc: Smooths the sub: nothing it adds goes much above this

Kicker.name: Mono sub
Kicker.desc: The same sub in both channels, from L+R. Off: each channel makes its own

Limit.name: Threshold
Limit.desc: How much the input is pushed up into the limiter

Limit.name: Ceiling
Limit.desc: The highest level the output reaches

Limit.name: Lookahead
Limit.desc: How early it starts to turn down before a peak. 0 ms is instant and can distort; the latency doesn't change

Limit.name: Link
Limit.desc: How much the two channels share their gain reduction. 100 % keeps the stereo image still; lower lets a peak on one side leave the other alone

Limit.name: Target
Limit.desc: Moves the red line on the LUFS meter. It doesn't change the sound

Limit.name: True peak
Limit.desc: Holds the points between samples under Ceiling too

Limit.name: Listen to removed
Limit.desc: Plays only what the limiter takes away

Limit.name: Oversampling
Limit.desc: Runs the limiter at a higher rate, which reduces aliasing when it works hard. Changes the latency

Limit.name: Oversampling filter
Limit.desc: Minimum phase has the least latency; linear phase keeps the phase of the highs. Changes the latency

Limit.name: Dither
Limit.desc: Adds very quiet noise for a bounce to a lower bit depth. Shaped moves it up where it's harder to hear. Only use it on the last plugin before a 16- or 24-bit bounce, and keep Ceiling at -0.1 dB or lower

Limit.name: Meter ballistics
Limit.desc: What the LUFS bar shows: short-term loudness, or plain RMS over 300 ms

MultiComp.name: Threshold
MultiComp.desc: Level where the band starts to act

MultiComp.name: Ratio
MultiComp.desc: Above 1:1 compresses. Below 1:1 raises the level above the threshold, by up to +24 dB

MultiComp.name: RMS size
MultiComp.desc: How long the detector averages. 0 is peak detection

MultiComp.name: Auto make-up
MultiComp.desc: Adds half the gain reduction a 0 dBFS level would get. It comes from Threshold, Ratio and Knee, so it can't pump. The amount shows in brackets after Gain

MultiComp.name: Auto release
MultiComp.desc: Recovers fast from transients and slowly from sustained compression

MultiComp.name: Feedback detect
MultiComp.desc: The detector listens to the band's output

MultiComp.name: Sidechain
MultiComp.desc: This band listens to the sidechain, filtered to the same range

MultiComp.name: Up threshold
MultiComp.desc: Level where the band starts to act

MultiComp.name: Up ratio
MultiComp.desc: At 1:2, a signal 20 dB below Up thresh is lifted by 10 dB. Type `2` or `1:2`

MultiComp.name: Max lift
MultiComp.desc: The most gain it ever adds

MultiComp.name: Floor
MultiComp.desc: No lift below it, fading in over the 8 dB above it

Room.name: Pre-delay
Room.desc: A gap before the reverb starts. With Sync pre-delay on, a note length instead

Room.name: Sync pre-delay
Room.desc: Pre-delay as a note at the host's tempo

Room.name: Size
Room.desc: How big the space is: the spacing of the early reflections and of the delays in the tail

Room.name: Decay
Room.desc: How long the tail takes to fall by 60 dB (RT60), at any Size

Room.name: Diffusion
Room.desc: How quickly the echoes blur into a smooth tail

Room.name: Mod
Room.desc: Slow movement of the delays in the tail, which keeps it from ringing

Room.name: Width
Room.desc: 0 is mono, 1 as it is, 2 wider; below 0 swaps the sides. The mono sum never changes

Room.name: Damping
Room.desc: How much faster the highs die away: their decay is Decay × (1 − 0.7 × Damping)

Room.name: Low cut
Room.desc: Takes the lows out of the reverb

Room.name: High cut
Room.desc: Takes the highs out of the reverb

Room.name: Freeze
Room.desc: Holds the tail

Room.name: Wet only (send)
Room.desc: Only the reverb comes out

Room.name: Ducking
Room.desc: Turns the reverb down while the dry signal plays: at 100 %, by 24 dB once the input is above −20 dBFS, and not at all below −50 dBFS. It comes back over about 300 ms

Room.name: Quality
Room.desc: Eco runs 8 delay lines for the least CPU. Normal runs 16; High adds smoother (cubic) modulation. On a change, the old tail rings out for up to 2 s while the new one starts, so nothing cuts off

Room.name: Early reflections
Room.desc: The level of the first echoes

Room.name: Stereo input
Room.desc: Mono-sum feeds the reverb the sum of both channels

Room.name: Wet
Room.desc: The reverb

Room.name: Dry
Room.desc: The untouched signal

Room.name: Mod rate
Room.desc: Scales the speed of every line's modulation: slow for a lush chorus, fast for shimmer. Mod still sets the depth

Room.name: Gate decay
Room.desc: How long the tail takes to fall by 60 dB (RT60), at any Size

Room.name: Auto gain
Room.desc: Trims the wet level as Size and Decay change, so a longer decay doesn't make the reverb louder. 0 dB at Size 55 % and Decay 1.8 s

Sature.name: Drive
Sature.desc: How hard the signal is pushed into the curve

Sature.name: Character
Sature.desc: Left: more even harmonics (2nd, 4th…), warm and full. Right: more odd ones (3rd, 5th…), edgier

Sature.name: Tone
Sature.desc: Tilts the saturated sound around 1 kHz: +6 is 3 dB brighter at the top and 3 dB less at the bottom

Sature.name: Low
Sature.desc: Below this, the signal passes clean

Sature.name: High
Sature.desc: Above this, the signal passes clean. Kept at least an octave above Low

Sature.name: Auto gain
Sature.desc: Keeps the loudness about the same at any setting

Sature.name: Dry
Sature.desc: The clean signal, for parallel saturation

Sature.name: Oversampling
Sature.desc: Higher is cleaner on bright, heavily driven sounds. Off has no latency but aliases more

Sature.name: Oversampling filter
Sature.desc: Linear phase has more latency. The clean and saturated signals stay lined up either way

Sature.name: DC filter
Sature.desc: Removes the offset an uneven curve can add

Verb.name: Width
Verb.desc: Stereo width of the wet signal

Verb.name: Max FFT
Verb.desc: The largest FFT used. 65536 is the lighter choice for long IRs

Verb.name: IR storage
Verb.range: Embed under 10 MB, Always embed, Path only
Verb.desc: Whether a project keeps its own copy of the IR

Chorus.name: Rate (synced)
Chorus.unit: choice, shown while Tempo sync is on
